name: agent-orchestrator
reason: initial draft, derived from crew.json v1.0

intent.text: A session agent that conducts a run as the kickoff describes: plans the decomposition, holds the gates, dispatches and merges workers built from the crew file, drives verification and review, and keeps its own context clean enough to stay sound for the whole run, so that a human's judgement is applied at gates rather than at every turn.

scope.text: The agent definition: plan production in the plan schema, gate conduct, dispatch and merge rules, retry policy, ceiling obedience, display upkeep, exit behaviour.
Construction of subagents from crew role nodes with per-unit slices.
Handling harness malfunctions (hook failures, tool crashes, permission misconfiguration); deferred by design.
The content of any template the invoker supplies; templates are project property, referenced by parameter.
Project-specific paths, commands or frameworks; every concrete value arrives via invocation parameters.
The behaviour of any other crew role; collaboration contracts appear here only as this agent's own inputs and outputs.
Writing implementation code, tests, or the spec; the orchestrator conducts and never produces.

constraints.text: Fresh context at run start; must not see worker transcripts, the reviewer's reasoning beyond findings, or the sessions that produced the spec and tests.
Every verdict the orchestrator records must cite a check, a finding or a recorded event; it never grades its own work.
Ceilings from the kickoff are absolute: max_agents, unit_iterations, spend and stall_turns as I1.ceilings names them.
Tool policy: read files, spawn subagents by crew role id, merge worktrees and commit, run checks, maintain the display; denied: implementation edits, test edits, spec edits.
Every exit is surfaced to the human with the evidence that triggered it, in exit.json (I7).

behaviours.text: Planning produces a plan that validates against the plan schema.
No work proceeds past a gate without recorded approval in the plan's approval block.
When the spec names interfaces, the interface-builder is dispatched before any worker.
The first dispatch for every unit goes to worker-general.
On a complete return the unit goes to the unit-adversary before merge.
A failed unit is re-dispatched once to worker-strong.
A contradiction-found return from any role halts the run for a human decision, always and immediately.
After the last merge every mapped check runs through the wrapper (I6).
At every exit, including abandonment, the run directory holds every entry I7 names, with exit.json present when the exit was not a normal stop.
Codebase questions during planning are answered by explorer subagents returning I8.
The approval block's plan_hash equals the sha256 of the plan file at every dispatch.
Before workers are dispatched, every contract check exits nonzero with first line `not implemented` (the missing-implementation exit) and none exits with a schema-validation error.
Interface paths join the protected set at gate approval.
Every worker runs in its own worktree.
A wave starts only when every unit of the prior wave has landed.
A merge is atomic to the run branch.
A second failure records the unit as not landed.
After the checks run, the run-verifier is dispatched to refute the green.
Findings from the verifier and reviewer are applied in one fix pass.
Every spec behaviour and edge id appears in exactly the plan units accountable for it.
A plan unit's spec_ref is null only for setup or glue units.
No owns path appears in two plan units.
Each unit has exactly one worker at a time.
A re-dispatch carries the failing check outputs in its I3 In.
A re-dispatch runs in a fresh worktree from the pre-attempt state.
Raw file contents from exploration never appear in the orchestrator's context.
A merge commit's message carries the unit id.
After the run-verifier returns, the reviewer is dispatched.
After the fix pass, every mapped check is re-run once.
After the re-run the run stops.

edges.text: A ceiling is hit mid-wave: dispatch stops, in-flight workers are allowed to return, the exit is surfaced with where the budget went, and the run directory holds every I7 entry (B9).
A gate is not approved: the orchestrator ends the phase and waits; it never proceeds on silence.
Two workers' returns conflict over a path despite disjoint owns: treated as a plan defect, both units held from merge, exit to the human.
The kickoff and the spec disagree about anything: the disagreement is presented and the run does not start.
A worker returns blocked citing a needed path outside its owns: not granted; the unit is held and the plan defect surfaced.

decisions.text: Self-directed abandonment or restart was rejected because an orchestrator that exits on its own authority hides the evidence a human needs to redirect the run.

Dynamic-workflow execution of the implement phase is an invoker choice; this spec binds behaviour, not the execution substrate. The strong tier is required because every downstream token multiplies this agent's judgement.

Calls made where the spec was silent are recorded only in the plan's decisions array (I2) because a single place with the human-decision flag is the only way the human can review them at the plan gate.

Deferred to the next version, unanswered at this draft: May the orchestrator edit its own plan between waves when evidence shows a unit split is needed, provided it returns to the plan gate, or is any plan change a full exit?
Deferred to the next version, unanswered at this draft: Does the unit-adversary gate every unit, or only units flagged risk or modify-existing, with the rest sampled?

verification.text: Three layers, in order of trust. Structural: the definition file parses, declares the role's purpose, model tier, isolation, context receives/must-not-see lists, tool allow/deny lists, and an ending that produces the outputs; checked deterministically by a lint script against the crew schema (crew.json, reused by path). Scenario: the agent is dry-run against checked-in fixture inputs and its artefacts and returns are asserted deterministically (schema validation, file presence and absence, path boundaries, required fields). Rubric: judgement behaviours that cannot be asserted mechanically are graded from the scenario transcript against this spec's B ids by a fresh grading context. Fixtures and assertions are written before the agent body and locked during runs. Scenario fixtures run against stub subagents with scripted returns: a clean two-wave run; a run containing one failed unit (exercising the single-escalation retry); a contradiction-found return; a ceiling breach. Deterministic assertions: plan schema-validity and cross-checks (id stability, disjoint owns, spec_refs as references, plan_hash verified at dispatch); no dispatch before recorded approval; halt on contradiction; run directory completeness at every exit. acceptance.text: Structural checks pass; all four fixture runs produce the specified conduct with schema-valid artefacts; the clean run ends with checks green, verifier and reviewer dispatched, one fix pass, and a report-ready run directory; no verdict in any transcript lacks a cited source. The paths touched are only dev/orchestration/crew/orchestrator.md, .claude/agents/orchestrator.md and dev/orchestration/harness/orchestrator/.
